mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form "X has more than Y" as a signed difference: X − Y = N (or as a variable difference if N is not given). Preserve the order and treat the difference as signed, not absolute.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement directly says "X has N more than Y" or "X has more than Y" without an explicit number.
mathgap.example: Misreading "Alice has more than Bob" as an absolute difference or ignoring the sign, leading to an equation like |Alice − Bob| = N instead of Alice − Bob = N.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor (including rational) interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "the number of X increases by k times" (k may be a fraction), treat it as multiplication: new X = original X × k.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any statement indicating a multiplicative increase rather than an additive one.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "the number of apples increases by 2 times" as new = old + 2 instead of new = old × 2.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer "X gives N to Y" occurs, subtract N from X and add N to Y, updating both counts simultaneously.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Applying "Alice gives 5 to Bob" as Alice = 5 and Bob = 0, instead of Alice −= 5, Bob += 5.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person and translate every relevant statement into a linear equation; then solve the resulting system of equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains multiple relational statements, differences, or transfers that together define a system of constraints.
mathgap.example: Skipping equation formulation and guessing a value for a person instead of setting up and solving the full linear system.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: If a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's final count to zero and give each recipient an equal share. For a redistribution between two people to equal amounts, set both to the average of their combined total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes a split‑all or an equal‑redistribution between participants.
mathgap.example: Treating a split‑all as each recipient receiving the original total instead of only a share, leaving the splitter with a non‑zero count.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret "difference between X and Y" as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order given, rather than as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions "difference between X and Y" (or similar phrasing).
mathgap.example: Reading "the difference between Alice and Bob is 5" as |Alice − Bob| = 5, which loses the sign information.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements (including conditional transfers) first, updating each person's count, before solving relational equations that involve those counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing all transfer‑related statements and before setting up or solving the system of equations.
mathgap.example: Solving a set of difference equations before applying a prior transfer, causing the equations to be based on outdated counts.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat direct count statements (e.g., "X has N items") as the initial amounts before any transfers, splits, or redistributions.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Assuming "Alice has 10 apples" is the final count even though later statements transfer apples to or from Alice.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: "The final answer is $\boxed{<integer>}$".
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the very end of the solution, before producing the final response.
mathgap.example: Returning "Answer: 20" or "20" instead of the required boxed LaTeX format.

mathgap.title: Cluster independent sub-systems
mathgap.principle: Identify groups of variables that are only linked among themselves (no equations or transfers connecting to other groups). Solve each group separately, then combine the results. This reduces the size of the linear system and avoids overwhelming the solver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many statements and variables, and you notice that some names appear only together in a subset of the equations.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve a huge, fully coupled system of dozens of equations at once, leading to errors or inability to find a solution, instead of breaking the problem into independent clusters.

mathgap.title: Complex difference phrasing handling
mathgap.principle: For statements like "the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to the difference between the number of A and B", interpret the left side as (Y − Z) and the right side as (A − B), preserving order, and treat both as signed differences (not absolute). This also covers simpler forms such as "Y has more than Z" and "difference between A and B".
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement combines "has more than" with a "difference between" clause, or any nested difference phrasing.
mathgap.example: Misreading "the number of broccolis that Valeria has more than Sam is equal to the difference between the number of Lilianna and Jimmie" as |Valeria − Sam| = |Lilianna − Jimmie|; the correct translation is Valeria − Sam = Lilianna − Jimmie.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that a direct count is the final amount, ignoring later transfers that modify the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as initial values before any transfers, splits, or redistributions, then apply those operations.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misreads "X gives N to Y" as "Y gives N to X", swapping giver and receiver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that "gives" means the giver loses N and the receiver gains N; update counts accordingly.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by k times' as addition
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing is confused with an additive increase, leading to adding k instead of multiplying.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat "increase by k times" as multiplication: new = old × k.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The condition is ignored or evaluated at the wrong point, causing the transfer to be applied unconditionally or incorrectly.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Evaluate the condition after all prior operations; apply the transfer only if the condition holds.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes differences are always non‑negative and drops the order information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order given in the statement and treat differences as signed (X − Y), not as absolute values.
